title: Freeman Nelson Jackson
repository: Delaware Native American Archives / Mitsawokett Collection
transcriber: Archival Transcriber / Written in the Genome
citation: "Freeman Nelson Jackson." Historical Document Record (2017). Preserved in the Nanticoke & Moor Historical Archive (Written in the Genome Collection).
lines: Freeman Nelson Jackson was born November 25, 1966 at Beebe Medical Center in Lewes, Delaware, and grew up in Millsboro, Delaware (the Thompsonville area). He was a lover and advocate of boxing; his all-time favorite was Muhammad Ali, and he attended the Boxing Hall of Fame, where he met Don King, Joe Frazier, Ken Norton, and Muhammad Ali. He was an amputee and a survivor of stage 4 cancer who made routine walks around Coverdale on crutches. He left this world on Monday, January 16, 2017 at Christiana Hospital in Wilmington, Delaware, at age 50. He leaves three children, Freeinna Jackson (23), Freeman Jackson Jr. (17), and Nevada Jackson (16); two stepchildren, Jason Long Jr. (24) and Desiree Thomas (26); one grandchild and one on the way; two sisters, Carla Jackson (54) and Darlene Kendrick (52); and one brother, Keith Jackson (48). He was preceded in death by his mother Mary Lingard, his stepfather George Lingard, his great niece Jade Showell, his brother Nelson Jackson a.k.a. Toe-Joe, his uncle Harry Jackson Jr., his grandfather Harry Jackson Sr., and his father Nelson Thompson.
